gen-dafont-dogica-gf-hedvig-letters-seri: Dogica's wide tracking gives its heavy letters real swagger. Hedvig Letters Serif, sturdy in the lowercase and open at every curve end, takes over below, so the loud heading hands off to something steadier.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-lisu-bosa: Dogica is heavy, wide-tracked and plainly in charge. Lisu Bosa, with spacious counters and gentle modulation, would carry paragraphs comfortably, its big lowercase keeping every word sturdy on the line.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-serif-hentaiga: Noto Serif Hentaigana brings open-jawed curves and mild stroke modulation, with small letters nearly as high as its capitals. And Dogica, heavy and widely spaced, gives the heading a commanding front door that the text beneath then follows quietly.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-ovo: Heavy and commanding, Dogica spreads its letters wide apart, with lowercase climbing almost to capital height. Ovo, a serif with slightly lighter thins, settles the loudness into something readable.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-domine: Playful and commanding, Early GameBoy stretches its letters out wide, with only a modest thick-thin difference between strokes. Early GameBoy grabs the eye; refined Domine holds the sentences steady.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-esteban: Esteban feels refined and classic, with thins barely slimmer than its stems. Early GameBoy, wide-tracked and playful, belongs up front in big, short bursts of text, where its commanding streak can show.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-halant: Halant feels sturdy and traditional, with outward-flaring terminals. Paragraphs in Halant settle into an authoritative rhythm, with the open-tracked, playful Early GameBoy waiting above to start things off.
